title: Optimal bound question
statement_text: Is it possible to decrease the bound $2n+1$ to $n$ in the following result: for every metric space $(X,d)$ of Assouad–Nagata dimension $n$ and every $f:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{Z}_+$, the family of intersection graphs of $f$-space-filling systems of subsets of $X$ has asymptotic dimension at most $2n+1$ (or at least in its special case: for every $\alpha\ge1$, the class of intersection graphs of systems of compact convex sets of aspect ratio at most $\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ has asymptotic dimension at most $2n+1$)?
context_text: For a cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a metric space $(X,d)$, its Lebesgue number is the supremum of $r\ge0$ such that every ball of radius $r$ lies in some member of $\mathcal{U}$, and its mesh is the supremum of the diameters of its members. A function $D:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is an $n$-dimensional control function for $X$ if for every $r>0$ there is a cover $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{U}_1\cup\dots\cup\mathcal{U}_{n+1}$ of $X$ with mesh at most $D(r)$, Lebesgue number at least $r$, and each $\mathcal{U}_i$ consisting of pairwise disjoint sets. The asymptotic dimension of $X$ is the least $n$ admitting such a $D$, and the Assouad–Nagata dimension is the least $n$ for which $D(r)=Kr$ works for some $K>1$ ($\mathbb{R}^n$ has Assouad–Nagata dimension $n$). A graph is viewed as the metric space of its vertices with the shortest-path distance, and a class of graphs has asymptotic dimension at most $n$ if a single $n$-dimensional control function works for all its members. The intersection graph of a system $\mathcal{S}$ of sets has vertex set $\mathcal{S}$, two sets being adjacent when they intersect. For $f:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{Z}_+$, $\mathcal{S}$ is $f$-space-filling if all its sets have finite diameter and for all $r,s>0$ and $x\in X$, the ball $B(x,r)$ meets at most $f(r/s)$ pairwise disjoint members of $\mathcal{S}$ of diameter at least $s$. The aspect ratio of $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ is its diameter divided by its height (the least distance between two parallel hyperplanes enclosing $S$). Without such fatness restrictions there is no bound: graphs obtained from bipartite graphs by subdividing each edge once are intersection graphs of boxes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ but have unbounded asymptotic dimension. The authors prove the upper bound $2n+1$ and remark that it is likely not optimal: interval graphs (intersection graphs of balls in $\mathbb{R}^1$) have asymptotic dimension $1$ rather than $3$. Since $n$-dimensional grids have asymptotic dimension $n$ and are touching graphs of balls in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the bound cannot go below $n$.
